The draft transportation and logistics product example is available here: https://github.com/Agrow-Labs/supply-chain-lib/blob/master/GS1-logistics.md

ms.report:
A. Output: The draft standards were presented to a group of 4 independent peers for review and feedback. Reviewers were asked to create an issue directly in the GitHub from their account in order to document that they willingly participated and provided their feedback.
A. Acceptance criteria:
・At least four (4) independent peers have been selected to provide review and feedback of the draft standards
・Proof from each reviewer that they have accepted the role/task/compensation agreement
・Each peer has provided feedback (in English) for each chosen standard (M1). A peer may provide feedback that they see no changes necessary to the standard. A "no change" review may be acceptable with proper rationale.

A. Evidence: Independent peer reviews/feedback on GitHub: https://github.com/Agrow-Labs/supply-chain-lib/milestone/1
B. Output: We have drafted a document that:
・Explains our peer selection criteria and why we chose the peers we did for their feedback and review
・Summarizes the feedback received
・Provides links to other areas (outside of GitHub issues) where we have participated in the on-going discussion around supply chain and logistics standards for Cardano.
・Summarizes the changes identified as necessary for Milestone #4

B. Acceptance criteria: Document should sufficiently cover the feedback provided, rationale for selection of the reviewers, and the next steps for the project.
B. Evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1hURfOj1ybKYsHmQ8pscSeMEjpduN1gkF/view?usp=sharing
C. Output: Brief YouTube video covering progress thus far
C. Acceptance criteria: Video covers the peer review feedback first impressions and next steps in a very quick and easily digestible fashion.
C. Evidence: https://youtu.be/1gvP54IA984
D. Output: Milestone #4 Revision Plan (PDF)

Note: Catalyst staff were contacted and shown proof of our attempts to reach out to the reviewer who failed to provide a final sign-off on the changes (all of their feedback was substantially addressed in our revisions). We were instructed that there is no need to publicly disclose proof of DMs/emails. We attempted to contact the reviewer and Charli3 multiple times beginning on January 02, 2026 when the updates were pushed to the GitHub.
